source.title: AdaSteer: Your Aligned LLM is Inherently an Adaptive Jailbreak Defender
source.authors: Weixiang Zhao; Jiahe Guo; Yu-Lin Hu; Yang Deng; An Zhang; Xing-Yu Sui; Xinyang Han; Yan-Yan Zhao; Bing Qin; Tat-Seng Chua; Ting Liu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some tables are flattened by PDF extraction, but their layout and values are generally readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study identifies a difference-in-means rejection direction and tests activation steering with it, but uses adaptive, dual-direction steering at selected layers rather than the original claim’s all-layer, all-position direction ablation and addition.
record.gate_note: The study measures rejection-direction and harmfulness-direction positions, steering strength, jailbreak defense, over-safety and utility. Values used to select layers or fit steering coefficients are not separately recorded as outcomes. Detailed per-attack DSR results are reported in Table 1 and later tables; the aggregate DSR rows below use the study’s own reported averages.
record.test_reason: A jailbreak-defense method paper, but its results bear on V1, V5 and V6. The 'w/o v_HD' ablation is addition along a difference-in-means refusal direction alone, and it raises refusal of jailbreak inputs. HD projections show complied jailbreaks still encoded as harmful. The RD is a variant: rejected minus complied harmful prompts, not harmful minus harmless. It is applied at a model-specific selected layer with fitted coefficients.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that adaptive steering along a rejection direction and a harmfulness direction, with input-dependent coefficients, defends against diverse jailbreaks while preserving utility. Note that the compliance vector is HD projected onto RD (Eq. 9), so the steering itself acts along one axis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means, but derives RD from rejected versus complied harmful instructions rather than harmful versus harmless instructions. Applies adaptive steering along RD and HD at selected layers; it does not perform the original claim’s all-layer, all-position ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: The selected layer differs by model and by direction. The authors report that Qwen2.5 does not clearly separate harmfulness positions on HD, unlike LLaMA-3.1 and Gemma-2. Steering coefficients are fit and adjusted using a validation set.

fits_no_version.finding: Rejection Law: complied jailbreak types positioned further against RD need larger steering coefficients to be refused (Table 2, Fig. 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How far a jailbreak pushes inputs against the refusal direction predicts how hard it is to defend.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the cataloged results. The interventions test adaptive steering at selected layers, not all-layer ablation of the naturally occurring direction. Utility is assessed using AlpacaEval win rate and over-safety compliance measures; these do not cover all model capabilities. The paper reports that HD positions do not clearly distinguish harmful and benign inputs for Qwen2.5.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the per-attack DSR rows from Table 1 and detailed per-attack and over-safety results in Tables 5-9, prioritizing aggregate outcomes, component ablations, HD position measurements, and multilingual results within the 60-row limit. Also omitted Gemma-2-27B-it over-safety CR values in Table 4 (84.80% to 89.20% on XSTest and 90.33% to 95.33% on OKTest).

untested.parts: Ablation of the direction to remove refusal; inducing refusal on harmless prompts; the harmful-minus-harmless recipe.
Whether attacks work by suppressing the direction; training against ablation.
All: the 'dual-direction' method steers along one axis, because v_HD is projected onto RD.
Transfer across models, variants, or from base to instruct.

missing.what: Qwen2.5-3B and 14B AdaSteer results (DSR 23.86→80.29, 59.57→93.71; win rates 45.72, 47.90)
'w/ reverse v_RD' ablation: replacing v_HD with negated v_RD keeps DSR but lowers utility
Per-attack DSR for RD-only addition (e.g. LLaMA Cipher 0→96)

record.verdict_notes: The record's V4 links are wrong: Eq. 9 makes v_HD a projection onto d_RD, so the RD/HD ablations do not show multiple refusal directions. Ablation-row baselines should be the unsteered model, not AdaSteer. There are small Table 3 versus Table 6 discrepancies (Qwen w/o RD win rate 48.82 vs 47.82; Gemma AdaSteer 85.86 vs 85.56). The steering layer is model-specific (Table 10) and the coefficients are tuned on a validation set. No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: Tests adaptive addition involving the rejection direction and reports defense and utility outcomes. Does not ablate the naturally occurring direction from every layer and position, test a single-direction-only addition as the full intervention, or test whether adding it makes harmless requests refused.
No weight edit or abliteration is evaluated.
Measures jailbreak inputs’ positions along the rejection direction but does not test whether attacks work by suppressing that direction or whether training against its ablation adds robustness.
Tests a two-direction steering method and component ablations. Does not establish that the model’s underlying refusal mechanism is an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
Compares harmfulness-direction positions for complied harmful and benign inputs; does not directly measure a separate harmfulness judgment or decision variable.

Tests multilingual attacks with directions applied to the evaluated models. Does not transfer one model’s direction to another model, compare base with instruct models, or establish transfer across model variants using a shared direction.
Does not compare refusal-training methods or training stages to determine when a removable direction exists.

source_check.condition: RD-only addition without the offsetting compliance term
source_check.reason: Over-safety CR falls on LLaMA (94.40->74.37) and Qwen (95.00->79.60). That is refusal induced on harmless prompts, which V1's addition arm predicts. The authors attribute the win-rate drop (45.72/36.37/33.08) to 'false rejections'. V1's abilities-kept part concerns ablation, which this study does not test, so it is untested rather than limited. On Gemma, CR rises to 90.17, so a 'CR falls' cost does not hold there. This could be merged into the first V1 verdict.

relation.reason: The ablations and the HD position analysis are results on the versions, not just use of the direction as a tool.

tranche.reason: This is a defense-method paper, but it reports more than its own method's performance. The RD-only ablation (w/o v_HD, Tables 3 and 6) and the HD projections of complied jailbreak versus benign inputs (Tables 2, 8, 9; section D.3) bear on V1, V5 and V6 in a new setting (jailbreak inputs, adaptive coefficients). T3 fits better than the reader's T2, because the study's question is defense, not whether refusal is mediated by one direction.

source_check.notes: AdaSteer steers at every layer and token position. v_HD is HD projected onto RD (Eq. 9), so all steering is along one RD axis. posHD values are unnormalized averages over complied inputs only, with no n per subset and no uncertainty, so they cannot be compared across models. Internal inconsistencies in the source: LLaMA Multilingual baseline is 22 (Table 1) vs 67 (D.5); Gemma AdaSteer average is 85.86 (Table 1) vs 85.56 (Table 6); Gemma AutoDAN posRD and posHD are both 30.39 in Table 9, possibly a copy error.

statements.correction: On LLaMA-3.1-8B, complied posHD for all 7 jailbreak sets is -12.78 to -25.55, including Multilingual at -14.74. Benign sets are 5.98 to 18.36 (Table 2). On Gemma-2-9B, the 7 jailbreak sets are 29.96 to 46.69, including Multilingual at 46.69, and benign sets are 64.90 to 78.68 (Table 9).
statements.problem: No numbers are given for this study. The description (AIM/AutoDAN/GCG on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B, correlational) is accurate. statements.correction: RD = mean(rejected harmful) minus mean(complied harmful) (Eq. 4), used directly as the steering vector. v_HD is HD projected onto RD (Eq. 9), so all steering acts along RD with adaptive lambda_r and lambda_c, at all layers.
statements.problem: This lists AdaSteer among transfer results that move something other than the difference-in-means direction. AdaSteer does steer along a difference-in-means direction. What differs is the contrast set (rejected vs complied harmful, not harmful vs harmless) and the input-dependent coefficients.
